entities.title: Apply a migration to production
entities.summary: Apply a game's new migration files by hand, before its pull request is merged and the game deployed.
entities.when: A pull request adds a file to a game's worker/migrations/, and the owner has asked for it to go live.
steps: In the game's folder, check that npx wrangler whoami names the repository's account; otherwise stop and ask the owner
Record a restore point: npx wrangler d1 time-travel info <database>, and copy the bookmark into a comment on the pull request
Apply each new migration file once, in filename order: npx wrangler d1 execute <database> --remote -y --file worker/migrations/<file>
Look at a table the migration changed
Add the acknowledgement line to the pull request's description
Merge. Merging deploys nothing: the game goes live when it is deployed by hand with npm run deploy in its folder
entities.verify: The Database migration check passes on the pull request.

entities.title: Check a game's migrations before deploying it by hand
entities.summary: No migration gate runs before a deploy any more, so whoever deploys checks that the database is ready for the code.
entities.when: Before npm run deploy in a game's folder that has a worker/schema.sql or worker/migrations/.
steps: Look for changes to worker/schema.sql or worker/migrations/ in the game's folder since it was last deployed
For each, check that its pull request acknowledges the migration; if not, apply it as in Apply a migration to production and acknowledge it on the merged pull request
Then deploy: npm run deploy in the game's folder
entities.verify: The game works against its database after the deploy.

entities.title: A database change reached main without a pull request
entities.summary: No pull request carries an acknowledgement, so nothing records that the migration was applied.
entities.when: A change to a game's worker/schema.sql or worker/migrations/ is on main with no pull request behind it.
steps: Apply the migration as in Apply a migration to production
Only then deploy the game by hand: npm run deploy in its folder
entities.verify: The game works against the migrated database after the deploy.

entities.title: A migration broke production
entities.summary: Restoring the bookmark undoes every write since it, so only the owner decides on it.
entities.when: A game misbehaves after its migration was applied.
steps: If the owner decides to restore: npx wrangler d1 time-travel restore <database> --bookmark=<bookmark>, in the game's folder
entities.verify: The game works against the restored database.
